data.question: Continue, pause or retire the Saturday forecast challenger after the calibration study quarantined mean_absret?
data.reasoning: The quarantine and the newly found rotation defect both undermine the CALENDAR statistic, not the forecasting evidence, which was measured with a valid paired bootstrap on two periods. The only decisive evidence for a forecast feature is prospective, and it can only be collected while issuing: pausing destroys irrecoverable observations, retiring discards a cheap test whose own evidence is intact. Expected information value is high (direct out-of-sample test of a plausible mechanism: weekend closure of traditional markets) at near-zero cost. The provenance is relabelled: forecasting evidence only; calendar support pending the corrected F-DOW test (amendment 4).
review_conditions: futility rule triggers -> retire that target automatically (journaled outcome)
corrected F-DOW test (amendment 4) does not support Saturday -> challenger continues on forecasting evidence alone; provenance label updated; no promotion argument may cite the calendar result
180 resolved pairs with CI below 0 -> eligible for HUMAN promotion review only
data.subject: CH:saturday_target_day

data.lesson: My first justification (left-tail as the clean remaining support) was wrong - that result came from the defective null too. Lesson: when a calibration shows a family-level excess, diagnose the family method before relying on ANY of its results, including the ones that look clean.
data.observed: Corrected F-DOW test (amendment 4, run c20261104T041145-dow4; method accepted on synthetic nulls 0/300, 2/300, 1/300): Saturday |return| lower SUPPORTED (disc -0.96pp p<=0.0002 BH 0.0056; conf -1.13pp one-sided p<=0.0002). Saturday left-tail REJECTED (BH 0.19). New: Sunday |return| lower and Monday |return| higher supported. The mean_absret quarantine was measured for the rotation method; under amendment 4 its own calibration gives 0,1,1/300 (within the frozen bounds), so it does not apply to F-DOW; it stays in force for F-DOM/F-MOY/F-TOM.
